main_body: Snow-covered sloped roof (rows ~7-50) over a log front wall with a double arched door, two lit windows and round wreaths (rows 52-76)
top_band: Pale white/blue-grey snow roof slope, rows ~8-50, with a lighter eave band at rows 47-50. It reads as a large surface seen from above.
evidence: Reading down the middle column, the roof slope is a tall, clearly visible top surface with horizontal snow-layer bands. A light eave edge at rows 47-50 ends it, and a dark shadow with icicles at rows 51-53 sits directly under it. Below that is the vertical plank wall with an arched door framed by iron straps and windows with snow sills. The structure matches the Beodeul reference houses, which also have a big roof slope above a shorter front wall. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The snow has about five steps (white, pale blue, blue-grey, mid blue, shadow blue) with small tuft marks and per-row shading. The wood wall has several browns with plank grain, icicles, lit windows, iron straps and wreaths. Outlines lean tinted: dark navy beside snow and dark brown beside wood, not neutral black. The roof's white areas are somewhat repetitive and a little flatter than the tile-by-tile reference roofs, so the density is slightly lower but acceptable next to the reference.
